intro: Before you stand The Three Tombs, in Erzurum province, from the 12th–14th century: three Saltukid tomb towers side by side. The oldest of them, that of Emir Saltuk, is taken as the beginning of the form in Anatolia.
history: The three tomb towers standing side by side here at Erzurum belong to the Saltukid period. The largest and oldest is that of Emir Saltuk, with its octagonal shaft and pyramid cap, and it is taken as the beginning of the form in Anatolia. Look closely at its body: bulls, snakes and eagles are carved there.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the tomb of Emir Saltuk with its octagonal shaft and animal reliefs, and then the other two towers beside it.
facts: Did you know? The tomb-tower form comes from the tents of Central Asia: its pointed cap is a felt tent translated into stone. And the oldest of the three, that of Emir Saltuk, is taken as the beginning of the tomb-tower form in Anatolia.
outro: This brings our journey to The Three Tombs to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These towers have kept their quiet company for centuries; let them keep it for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
